title: Request Scavenger Diary and Priority Playlets — Sept 2026
content:
TL;DR:
A two-week field sweep across 18 enterprise customers and 12 fast-growing startups surfaced 27 distinct asks. Five themes dominate: latency tail events, KV/prefix cache surprises, guidance for quality/cost tradeoffs, rollout ergonomics (canary/rollback), and better observability for token-level cost. This doc captures raw vignettes, synthesized asks, proposed low-effort 'playlets' (micro experiments), risk notes, and next actions. Aim: fast wins for Q4 and hypothesis-driven experiments to de-risk bigger investments.

Methodology:
- Window: 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-10
- Sources: support tickets (triaged), CS calls, 1:1s with dev champions, product usage telemetry, three customer-run load tests, and Slack threads.
- Inclusion rule: any repeated ask across >=2 customers or high-severity single-customer blocker qualifies for a playlet.

Raw vignettes (representative):
1) "RetailGen" (large e-comm): intermittent 95th p90->p99 latency spikes when using stream + tools; spikes correlate with longer prompt prefixes. They repeatedly bypass batchers.
Quote: "We have to fall back to smaller models in bursts — this wastes engineering cycles."

2) "FinReview" (regulated financial): worried about embeddings costs — they run nightly similarity scans and saw token costs double after a prompt redesign. They asked for deterministic cost estimates for reranking flows.

3) "DocsFlow" (SaaS): rolling out a new assistant, wants canary rollout that splits by customer org and auto-rolls back on quality regressions measured over evaluation prompt set. Current guidance is manual and slow.

4) "HealthAI" (on-prem private): KV cache invalidation after minor schema change caused a high volume of regenerations. They want clearer debugging hooks for cache misses + suggested config defaults for private deployments.

5) "StartUpX" (early stage): wants a simple SDK helper that selects model variant for given cost/latency target (e.g., budget=50% of hosted standard). They described engineer time wasted building naive heuristics.

Synthesis — Themes & Representative Asks:
A. Latency tail events (frequency: high, pain: high)
- Asks: better tooling to identify tail drivers (sequence length, kernel fallback), automatic suggestion to enable prefix caching, per-route tail SLO reporting.
- Customer impact: frequent consumer-facing timeouts; manual mitigations (downgrade model) used as stopgap.

B. KV / prefix cache visibility & ergonomics (frequency: medium, pain: high for private/dedicated)
- Asks: expose sample cache metrics (hit/miss ratio by route, prefix distribution), per-tenant cache config snapshots, one-click cache flush with audit log, and cache warm-up helpers.
- Customer impact: costly surges when cache warms or invalidates; engineers spend hours tracing.

C. Cost/quality tradeoff primitives (frequency: high, pain: medium)
- Asks: model selector SDK, guided quantization recommendations per workload, exportable cost-estimation runbooks for common patterns (reranker, summarizer, chat).

D. Rollouts & regression detection (frequency: medium, pain: medium-high)
- Asks: first-class canary by org/region, automatic evaluation against a customer prompt set (synthetic or uploaded), auto-rollback triggers for quality regressions beyond threshold.

E. Token-level observability (frequency: high, pain: medium)
- Asks: token-level cost breakdown in console, per-request token diagnostics (where tokens were spent: system, user, assistant, tool), and exportable traces to link with customer's billing.

Proposed Playlets (fast experiments / microproducts):
1) Tail Investigator (2-week spike):
- What: a small diagnostic agent that runs through recent p95/p99 traces and surfaces correlated features (prompt length, model variant, whether KV hit) + a one-click suggested mitigation (enable prefix caching on that route or pin shorter context).
- Outcome metric: reduce manual triage time for tail incidents by 60% in pilot customers.
- Risk/Deps: needs access to traces; SRE involvement to fetch traces. Low infra risk.
- Owner: eng-solutions + observability.

2) KV Snapshot UI + Flush (4-week MVP):
- What: console surface that shows per-route cache hit/miss heatmap for last 24h, plus a guarded flush button with audit entry.
- Outcome metric: decrease cache-related support tickets by 40% among private/dedicated customers.
- Risk: cache state is sensitive; require RBAC and audit log.
- Owner: product-console + private-deployments.

3) Model Selector SDK (3-week alpha):
- What: a tiny SDK helper that accepts budget/latency constraints and returns a ranked set of model variants + estimated per-request cost (based on our perf profiles).
- Outcome metric: reduce number of customer self-built selectors and follow-up support threads. Pilot with StartUpX and RetailGen.
- Owner: devx + product-hosted-api.

4) Canary Eval Runner (6-week scoped):
- What: pipeline to run uploaded prompt sets (or sampled canonical prompts) against candidate model/version on canary traffic and compute a small set of quality deltas (ROUGE, embed-sim-based drift). Add an opt-in auto-rollback.
- Outcome metric: reduce time-to-detect quality regressions for rollouts from days to hours for pilot customers.
- Risk: governance needed for customer-uploaded prompt privacy.

5) Token Cost Breakdowns (4-week):
- What: augment per-request logs with token-category labels and add breakdown view in console and CSV export.
- Outcome metric: number of customers using breakdown to optimize prompts (target: 8 pilot customers).
- Owner: console + billing.

Prioritization Rationale (short):
- Quick wins: Tail Investigator and KV Snapshot UI = high customer pain, relatively low infra change, immediate impact on CS ticket volume.
- Strategic investments: Canary Eval Runner and Model Selector SDK = higher effort but unlocks safer rollouts and persistent cost savings.

Engineering blockers & notes:
- Access to traces and token labeling requires small contract changes for hosted vs private deployments (scoped infra work to ensure privacy for uploaded prompts).
- KV Snapshot UI must be gated by RBAC; private deployments may need a different collection agent.
- Model perf profile library needs vetting against long-tail models; we should seed with top 8 models used by revenue customers.

Quick timeline proposal (Q4):
- Weeks 1–2: build Tail Investigator prototype and run with 3 customers (RetailGen, StartUpX, DocsFlow).
- Weeks 3–6: KV Snapshot UI prototype + guarded flush for private pilot; Model Selector SDK alpha.
- Weeks 7–12: Canary Eval Runner scoping and token-breakdown launch for hosted console.

Success metrics (aligned to customer impact):
- Reduce cache-related support tickets by 40% for pilot customers inside 30 days.
- Decrease manual tail incident triage time by 60% for engaged customers.
- 70% of pilot customers adopt Model Selector SDK recommendations at least once in first 3 weeks.

Open questions / unresolved trade-offs:
- Should auto-rollback be opt-in at org-level or global per deployment?
- How granular should token labeling be to balance value vs storage/billing overhead?
- What privacy guardrails for customer-uploaded prompt evals (encryption at rest, ephemeral storage, redaction)?

Next actions (owners & dates):
- Maya: Schedule 60-min pilot kickoff with RetailGen + StartUpX (target: 2026-09-23).
- Liam: prototype Tail Investigator and share a demo trace by 2026-09-27.
- Priya: draft RBAC/audit requirements for KV flush by 2026-09-30 and coordinate with private-deployments lead.
- Ben: scope cost for perf-profile library and list top 8 models by 2026-09-24.

Appendix — Short customer notes (raw):
- RetailGen: "We have a user-visible spinner. It kills our conversion metrics. Need a quick way to detect why one route suddenly spikes."
- FinReview: "We redesigned prompts and overnight our bill doubled — need estimate tooling before we ship prompt changes."
- DocsFlow: "A/B testing rollouts without rollbacks gives us headaches. We will delay launches if rollback is manual."

If you want this spun into a short-playbook or a one-pager for execs, I can prepare a condensed version with estimated eng points and prioritized roadmap.

— Maya
